issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] Case-folding asymmetry between the two judgment layers. The legacy string layer matches ASK_PATTERNS with `grep -qiE` (case-insensitive — hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:2924,2926), while the Layer 3.3 token axis that F65 introduced to REPLACE string anchors compares normalized tokens case-sensitively against `CONTROL_PLANE_NAMES` (:1236-1243). Consequence: a target spelled `.CLAUDE` is gated only for the verbs the old regexes happen to cover (`rm`), and is allow for every verb that exists only on the new axis (`find … -delete`, `mv`, `rmdir`, `find … -exec rm -rf {} +`). On macOS (the platform this harness documents itself running on; default APFS is case-insensitive) those commands destroy the real control plane. Measured: `rm -rf .CLAUDE` ask (reason names the old string pattern `\brm\b…\.claude…`), `find .CLAUDE -delete` allow + whole `.claude` dir gone in the lab, `mv .CLAUDE /tmp/sink` allow + dir gone, `rmdir .CLAUDE` allow, `{find,.CLAUDE,-delete}` allow + dir gone, `bash -c "find .CLAUDE -delete"` allow + dir gone. The new axis is strictly weaker than the axis it replaced on this dimension — a regression in coverage introduced when the axis changed, not a notation nobody thought of.

[security][critical][confidence:high] Trailing `/.` is never folded. `normalize_path_token()` folds `//`, `/./` and trailing `/`, and folds an internal `seg/../`, but none of those rules has a trailing-form counterpart: `.claude/.` stays `.claude/.` and misses the exact-match case. Lab-confirmed live damage: `find .claude/. -delete` → allow, `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/hooks/guard.sh` deleted (`find` errors on the `.` component itself but deletes the contents first). Same for `.claude/./.`, `./.claude/.`, `.claude//.`, `.claude/.//.`, `$PWD/.claude/.`, `.claude/./hooks/.`, `hooks/.` (deleted `hooks/hooks.json`). `rm -rf .claude/.` is also allow but is harmless in practice (`rm: "." and ".." may not be removed`) — the damage comes through `find` and `find -exec`.

[security][critical][confidence:high] Trailing `..` from a child is never folded, for the same structural reason: the fold regex is `([^/]+)/\.\./` and requires the closing slash. `.claude/hooks/..` and `.claude/./hooks/..` therefore stay unfolded and reach allow, while `.claude/hooks/../` (one character longer) is correctly ask. Lab: `find .claude/hooks/.. -delete` → allow, `.claude/settings.json` + `.claude/hooks/guard.sh` deleted; `{find,.claude/hooks/..,-delete}` identical. `find .claude/*/.. -delete` → allow, same damage.

[criteria][high][confidence:high] The generated suite still cannot emit any of the above, by construction — the same meta-defect the 39th verdict named, one notch further down. `cp_notations()` (tests/pre-bash-firewall-generated.bats:238-241) returns exactly `$x`, `./$x`, `$x/`, `x/../$x`, `a/b/../../$x`, `$x/../$x`, `./x/.././$x`. Every leak found this round is a notation that is *adjacent to a rule the normalizer already implements* (`/./` has no `/.` case; `/../` has no `/..` case; the string layer is case-insensitive and the token layer is not). The pool should be generated FROM the normalizer's own transformation set — for each fold rule, emit its prefix / infix / suffix / repeated / case-varied forms — rather than hand-listed next to it. Until the pool derives from the code, the suite's 'every generated cell is ask/BLOCKED or attributed' property stays vacuously satisfiable (SC-11(2) gap the 39th already wrote down).

[quality][medium][confidence:medium] The INVARIANTS addendum claims the parity invariant 'would have caught both the 38th and 39th leaks' and that because it is an equivalence rather than an enumeration 'new notations are covered automatically'. The second half is not true as implemented: the parity test compares literal vs. brace for notations drawn from the hand-list, so a notation absent from the list is covered by neither side. missing_criteria: The notation axis needs a **same-target equivalence** criterion, not a literal/brace parity criterion: 'for any spelling S that the shell and filesystem resolve to control-plane location L, the decision for <verb> S equals the decision for <verb> L.' Parity (literal vs. brace) cannot catch this round's leaks because both sides are allow. The equivalence form would catch case, trailing `/.`, trailing `/..`, and whatever spelling comes next.

The notation pool must be **derived from the guard's own fold table** rather than hand-listed: for each rule in `normalize_path_token()` (`//`, `/./`, `seg/../`, leading `./`, trailing `/`, trailing glob), generate its prefix / infix / suffix / doubled / interleaved forms, and add a case-variation factor on filesystems where `[[ -d .CLAUDE ]]` holds for `.claude`. SC-11(2) currently lets an under-generating rule satisfy itself vacuously — the 39th already wrote this down and it was not implemented.

No criterion requires the two judgment layers (string ASK_PATTERNS with `grep -qiE`, token Layer 3.3 with case-sensitive comparison) to agree on case sensitivity, or more generally requires the replacement axis to be a superset of the axis it replaced. 'The new axis must not be weaker than the string anchors it retired on any dimension' is a checkable invariant: for every ASK_PATTERN that names a control-plane literal, the token axis must gate the same command with the verb set widened.
ambiguous_criteria: `ancestor_directory_operand`'s boundary is still unstated in the direction the 39th asked for. It says the operand judge recognizes 'the control plane itself and its notation variants', which is exactly what `.claude/.`, `.claude/hooks/..` and `.CLAUDE` are — yet the guard does not gate them, and no other key claims them. Add the sentence the 39th proposed: a path whose canonical resolution IS the control plane is never an ancestor-operand residual.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-11(2) still accepts 'all generated cells gated or attributed' with no coverage obligation on the generator's pools. Three consecutive rounds of leaks have come from under-generation, not from ungated generated cells.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Next iteration, narrow scope: (a) fold trailing `/.` and trailing `/..` in `normalize_path_token()` (the fold rules need suffix counterparts; simplest is to append a `/` sentinel before folding and strip it after, so `/./` and `/../` rules see the trailing forms); (b) make the control-plane comparison case-insensitive when the filesystem is case-insensitive, or unconditionally (a case-insensitive match can only over-gate, and `rm` is already case-insensitive via the string layer, so the asymmetry has no upside); (c) rewrite `cp_notations()` to generate from the fold table plus a case factor, and add the same-target equivalence assertion against the canonical form's decision; (d) fix the over-budget ask reason string. Do not re-open the brace-leaf `..` fix, the cap-exit pinning, or the `.mcp.json` residual — all three verified closed here.
